title: MOXIR 17.10 — Minimal — the show patch
howToRead: docs/architecture/RIG_BUILD.md §20. The LD's patch plan as data: which universe each position runs on, where each block starts, the fixture numbers and the DMX mode per type. scripts/rigbuild/patch-plan.mjs applies it to the project document (the single truth); patch.mjs --exact makes the desk agree; patch-sheet.mjs prints the crew's sheet. Never edit addresses in the document or on the desk by hand — change this file and run the three again.
method: Blocks select lamps from the DOCUMENT — by type, height (lens above/below 3 m = in the air / on the floor) and side — never by the name of a truss, so a re-hang (a new crane shape) re-runs to a correct patch. Positions and hung/standing come from the document, except the column rows, where the plan adds the side (HL/HR) to the name.

One universe per data run from the node: the crane line (in the air, one cable up the hoist), each side wall of the hall (so no DMX cable crosses the dance floor), and the booth. Four runs = the four ports of one 4-port Art-Net node.
Blocks start on round numbers (001, 101, 201 …) and the fixture number says where a lamp is: hundreds = its universe, tens = its block. A crew reads U2.101 and fixture 211 as the same lamp.
Within a block lamps go in the order a crew walks the position: along the crane line from house left to house right (−x to +x); along a wall from the DJ end outwards (z up).
A 16-bit fixture is always whole inside one universe (every block is checked against 512).
Each universe keeps at least half of its 512 channels spare, so a lamp added on the night takes the next free address in its own block without moving anything.

Mode per type: the maker's own mode where the maker lists one (UP-B380F 16ch, UP-PL5403 8ch — both single-mode units); otherwise the fewest channels that still give what the looks use. Where the maker's channel ORDER is not published, the desk runs the ASSUMED test list of the same footprint (RIG_BUILD.md §19.1) and the crew sets the maker's mode on the unit.

node.what: one 4-port Art-Net node at the booth (planning equivalent: Luminex LumiNode 4 — the rental list has DMX splitters UP-PDU60A/B but no node)
node.protocol: Art-Net 4 (sACN E1.31 also possible — the desk sends either)
node.numbering: desk universe U1 = Art-Net Port-Address 0 (Net 0 · Sub-Net 0 · Universe 0) = sACN universe 1; U2 = Port-Address 1 = sACN 2; and so on
node.splitters: a DMX splitter (the rental house's UP-PDU60B, IP-rated) where a run branches; every run ends in a 120 Ω terminator

HL.label: house left (x < 0, NE wall) — the audience's left, facing the DJ

HR.label: house right (x > 0, SW wall) — the audience's right, facing the DJ

up-b380f.why: the maker lists one mode, 16 channels (uplight.com.cn UP-B380F page, '16通道模式', and the made-in-china listings); pan/tilt 16-bit is in it. Its channel ORDER is not published: the desk runs the ASSUMED 16ch list (UPlus 380 IP BEAM).

up-pl5403.why: the maker lists ONE mode, 8 channels (uplight.com.cn UP-PL5403 page, '通道模式：8通道模式', checked 2026-09-29) — so 8ch, whatever the looks need. Its channel ORDER is not published: the desk runs the ASSUMED 8ch list (UPlus IP PAR-54X3: dimmer, R, G, B, W, strobe, function, speed) until the rental unit's chart is read.

ext-strobe.why: not chosen yet (another supplier). Planned on the Martin Atomic 3000 4-channel mode (intensity, duration, rate, effects) — the looks use intensity and rate. Blocks are spaced so a unit of up to 4 channels needs no re-address.

ext-hazer.why: not chosen yet (another supplier). Planned on a 2-channel hazer (haze output, fan) — both needed.

the UP-PL5403 in the air, grazing the crane bridge

universes.run: node port B → along the house-left (NE, x < 0) column row, DJ end outwards

universes.label: House right wall (SW)
universes.run: node port C → along the house-right (SW, x > 0) column row, DJ end outwards
